page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter · 2 marks

steps.label: The definition
steps.mark_note: Minimum energy to remove an electron
lines: The work function of a metal is the minimum
energy needed to just remove an electron
from the surface of the metal.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The word minimum is part of the definition, not an extra.
steps.why: An electron can be removed by giving it any energy above a certain lowest value. The work function is that lowest value, so without the word minimum the definition does not pick out one energy.
common_mistakes: Leaving out minimum. Any larger energy also removes the electron; the work function is the smallest one that does.
Saying energy to move an electron inside the metal. It is the energy to remove it from the surface.

recall.must_convey: That the work function is the minimum energy needed to just remove an electron from the metal surface.
accept: to remove an electron from the surface
smallest energy to make an electron leave the metal

steps.memory_tip: Three words carry the mark: minimum, remove, surface.

steps.label: Symbol and unit
steps.mark_note: W₀ or φ₀, measured in eV
lines: It is written as W₀ or φ₀ and is usually
Each metal has its own work function value.

lines.text: W₀: minimum energy to remove an electron

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Give the symbol, the unit eV, and say the value depends on the metal.
steps.why: Work functions are a few electron volts — about 2 eV for caesium and near 6 eV for platinum — so eV is the natural unit, and the value is a property of the metal.
common_mistakes: Writing joule as the usual unit. Joule is correct but the values are a few eV, and eV is what the examiner expects here.
Saying every metal has the same work function. The value differs from metal to metal.

recall.must_convey: That the work function is written W₀ or φ₀, is measured in electron volt, and depends on the metal.
reject: minimum energy to remove an electron

steps.memory_tip: Symbol W₀, unit eV, and the value belongs to the metal.

insider_note: The book's own line here is misprinted; what earns the mark is minimum energy, to just remove an electron, from the metal surface — then W₀ and eV.
